edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber II 3

source_text: Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie. Meridies plena lux et perfecta scientia est. Sponsa non vult errare inter greges sodalium — haereses et doctrinas varias — sed in ipso meridie Verbi pascua invenire. Si non indicaverit sponsus, periclitatur anima post vestigia gregum alienorum abire.
pass_a_gloss: Indicate to-me whom loves soul my, where you-may-pasture, where you-may-lie at-noon. Noon full light and perfect knowledge is...
pass_b_english: [[Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you pasture, where you lie down at noon >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:7]]. Noon is full light and perfect knowledge. The Bride does not want to wander among the flocks of companions — heresies and varied teachings — but to find the Word’s pastures at noon itself. If the Bridegroom does not show her, the soul is in danger of going after the tracks of alien flocks.
